## Overview
Mount Guinsayawan (also known as Tipasi/Tepasi) is a prominent volcanic peak within the Cuernos de Negros volcanic complex in Negros Oriental, Philippines. With an elevation of approximately 1,788-1,821 meters, it is one of the major peaks in the complex, which has a base diameter of 36 kilometers. The mountain is located inside Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park.

## Volcanic Complex
Mount Guinsayawan is part of the Cuernos de Negros ('Horns of Negros') volcanic complex, classified by PHIVOLCS as a potentially active volcano. The complex includes several prominent peaks: Mount Talinis (1,862m - the tallest), Magaso, Guinsayawan, Yagumyum Peak, and Guintabon Dome. The mountain range is highly fumarolic with solfataras and steam vents on its slopes, harnessed for geothermal electricity generation.

## Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park
The mountain is situated within the 8,016-hectare Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park, covering the municipalities of Valencia, Sibulan, and San Jose. The park protects about 3,462 hectares of forest spread over the Guintabon, Kabalin-an, and Guinsayawan mountain ranges. In 2024, the ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity listed this park among Southeast Asia's topnotch nature reserves.

## Biodiversity
The area surrounding Mount Guinsayawan is the only remaining rainforest in Negros Island. It hosts 237 plant species, 124 fern species, and 114 bird species, many of which are threatened. Notable wildlife includes the Visayan wrinkled-billed hornbill, Negros striped babbler, Negros bleeding-heart pigeon, glossy swiftlet, indigo-banded kingfisher, monkeys, leopard cats, and monitor lizards.

## Nearby Attractions
The Twin Lakes (Lake Balinsasayao and Lake Danao) are the park's main attractions, rising 1,000 feet above sea level. Activities include boat riding (P250/hour), kayaking (P150/hour), trekking, camping, and visiting Olayan Waterfall. Swimming is prohibited as the lakes are a major water source for the city. Guided tours are available for P300 per group of three.

## How to Get There
From Dumaguete City, the Twin Lakes Natural Park is approximately 14.5 km away (about 1 hour). Rent a scooter or motorbike, or take a bus going north and alight at the bus stop going to Twin Lakes, then hire a habal-habal. Entrance fees are P50 for Filipinos and P100 for foreigners. The park has facilities including a view deck, cottages, restaurant, souvenir shop, and visitor center.
